transcript.text: dyson keeps pulsin on n off like its stutterin, wont stay on proper. batt is full. pls help

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. That stuttering on/off behaviour is usually the vacuum's protection system kicking in because it senses restricted airflow. It’s trying to stop itself from overheating or damaging the motor. Since you’ve confirmed the battery is full, the most common causes are a blockage somewhere in the air path (hose, wand, or floorhead) or filters that are clogged or still damp from washing. Please try these steps:
1. Empty the bin completely.
2. Detach the wand and floorhead. Look through them to ensure nothing is stuck inside (like a coin or large debris). If you have a Dyson stick model, check the inlet where the wand connects to the main body.
3. Remove the pre-motor filter and HEPA filter (if your model has one). Wash them in cold water only—no detergent—and let them dry for at least 24 hours. Even slight dampness will cause pulsing.
4. Reassemble everything and try it again on normal mode (not Boost/Max). If it runs steadily now, the issue was a blockage or damp filter. If it still stutters with clear airways and dry filters, let me know exactly which Dyson model you have so I can guide you further.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
its a v8 animal. emptied the bin, was full of dog hair, still pulsin tho. no burning smell or heat btw

We need to look at the two other things that make a Dyson stutter: damp filters or a hidden blockage. 1. Filters: Even if they looked okay, if they were washed recently and not bone-dry for 24 hours, they will choke the airflow and cause pulsing. If you haven't washed them yet, please do so now (cold water only) and leave them to dry completely before trying again. 2. Blockages: Dog hair can get stuck in the wand or the floorhead neck. Detach the wand and look through it; drop a coin in one end—if it doesn't fall straight out of the other, there's a blockage. Also check the floorhead brush bar area for tangled hair. Please let me know if you've done these checks and what you found.

filter has never been washed, didnt know u could lol its grey not purple. wand had a big clump of hair n cat litter stuck at the bottom where the head goes on, pulled it out. brush bar had a bit of hair, cut it off

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. Since it’s still pulsing, we need to look at the filters. You mentioned they’ve never been washed. Even if they look okay, Dyson filters trap very fine dust that isn't always visible until you hold them up to a light. More importantly, if they were ever damp (even slightly) or just haven't been washed in years, they are likely choking the airflow. 1. Remove both filters from the main body.
2. Do not use soap.
3. Shake out the excess water and leave them somewhere warm and dry for at least 24 hours. They must be completely dry before you put them back in, or it will cause exactly this pulsing issue. While they are drying, please check the inlet on the main body (where the wand connects). Look inside with a torch to ensure no large debris is stuck there blocking the air from reaching the motor. Let me know if it stays on steadily or if it still stutters.
ok washed the filter, water came out black. left it overnight on the radiator side. pulses way less now but still a bit. checked the inlet on the body too, bit dusty so wiped it

That’s good progress—the fact that it pulses less now suggests the filters were the main choke point. 1. Check the floorhead: Detach the wand from the floorhead (the part with the brush bar). Turn the vacuum on briefly and hold your hand over the large opening where the wand connects to the head. You should feel a very strong, steady blast of air. If it feels weak or intermittent, there is a blockage inside the floorhead itself (often small items like cat litter grains get sucked into the mechanism).
2. Check the filter dryness: Even if they look dry, filters can hold moisture deep inside for longer than 12 hours, especially in humid rooms. If you have another day to spare, leave them in a warm, dry place (not on a radiator, which can warp plastic) for a full 24-36 hours total. Please try the floorhead airflow check first and let me know what you feel.
did the wand thing already, big clump of hair n litter was at the bottom where head goes on, pulled it out. now with dry filter its fine, proper suction no pulsin

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. That is excellent news. It sounds like the combination of the heavy blockage in the wand and the very dirty filters were triggering the vacuum's safety protection, causing it to stutter. To help keep it running smoothly for longer:
1. Try to empty the bin more frequently when dealing with pet hair, as even a partially full bin can reduce airflow.
2. Wash the filters every month or so (once they are completely dry again) rather than waiting until they look black. If you have any other questions about your Dyson V8 Animal, just let me know.

candidates: Blocked airflow (hose, wand, filter, or bin inlet) (high)
Damp or clogged filters causing protection mode (medium)
Battery contact issue or low charge despite indicator (low)
